name: Reference soil Uruguay 1
summary: A seasonally waterlogged Planosol from the rice-growing lowlands of eastern Uruguay. A pale, leached upper soil stops abruptly on a dense clay subsoil that perches water, producing iron mottles, manganese nodules and grey reduced streaks.

info.Location: Cerro Largo, Uruguay (10 km S of Rio Branco)

credit: Photo: ISRIC World Soil Reference Collection, CC BY-SA 3.0 https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:ISRIC_monolith_UY-001.jpg — Site and horizon data condensed from ISRIC – World Soil Information https://isis.isric.org/monoliths/reference-soil-uy001 — Feature notes written for this site.

horizons.name: Ah
horizons.description: Dark grayish brown (10YR 4/2 moist) loam; massive to weak medium subangular blocky structure; friable; common fine faint mottles; few small hard Mn concretions; smooth boundary.

horizons.name: E
horizons.description: Dark grayish brown (10YR 4/2 moist), light brownish gray (10YR 6/2 dry) loam; massive to weak platy structure; friable; common fine faint mottles; abrupt broken boundary.

horizons.name: Btg1
horizons.description: Grayish brown (10YR 4.5/2 moist) clay loam; strong medium prismatic to angular blocky structure; firm; many coarse prominent strong brown (7.5YR 5/6) mottles; continuous thick clay cutans; few small soft Mn nodules; gradual smooth boundary.

horizons.name: Btg2
horizons.description: Grayish brown (10YR 4.5/2 moist) clay loam; strong coarse prismatic to angular blocky structure; very firm; common medium prominent strong brown (7.5YR 5/6) mottles; broken moderately thick clay cutans; very few Mn nodules; diffuse wavy boundary.

horizons.name: Btg3
horizons.description: Grayish brown (2.5Y 5/2 moist) clay loam; strong coarse wedge-shaped angular blocky structure; very firm; broken moderately thick clay cutans; many small soft Mn nodules; diffuse smooth boundary. (Designation assigned here.)

horizons.name: C
horizons.description: Light brownish gray (2.5Y 6/2 dry) clay loam; moderate medium angular blocky structure; extremely hard (dry); broken thin clay cutans; few large hard Mn nodules; very few gypsum nodules.

features.title: Grass root mat
features.description: Dense fibrous roots in the topsoil.

features.title: Leached E horizon
features.description: Pale layer from which clay and iron have been removed by lateral flow of perched water above the clay subsoil.

features.title: Abrupt textural change
features.description: Loam sits directly on clay loam. Water collects on this boundary after rain, which keeps the upper soil wet and reducing.

features.title: Prism crack
features.description: Vertical crack between prisms in the dense Btg horizon.

features.title: Manganese spots
features.description: Black Mn oxide spots. They form where manganese, mobilized while the soil is saturated, re-oxidizes as it dries (a redox concentration).

features.title: Fe–Mn nodule
features.description: Rounded black iron–manganese nodule. Repeated wetting and drying cycles build these up layer by layer.

features.title: Iron mottle
features.description: Yellowish-brown iron oxide mottle, a redox concentration formed where oxygen reaches the soil along cracks and pores.

features.title: Grey streak (redox depletion)
features.description: Grey zone along a crack where iron was reduced and carried away by water.
